description: Sixteen original modern Hebrew prose works by four independently catalogued authors. These are cross-work controls for the Hebrew-script feature pipeline, not a Biblical Hebrew benchmark.
selection_protocol: Before inspecting classifier scores, choose four original prose works of 3000 to 30000 normalized tokens per author from four late nineteenth/early twentieth century Hebrew writers. Inspect catalogue entries and openings for shared modern social/psychological fiction. Exclude translated works, duplicate editions, biblical/historical retellings and folklore collections, or records with editorial prefaces whose voice cannot be separated confidently. Prefer earliest eligible catalogue IDs for Brenner, Gnessin and Bershadsky; for Berdyczewski choose four eligible modern stories after inspecting the first 65 prose records. Eligibility applies to the extracted body, not publisher text. This is a convenience sample, not a preregistered representative author sample.
attribution_caveat: Modern Hebrew is separated by centuries and substantial linguistic, literary, editorial and transmission differences from Biblical Hebrew. Results cannot establish scriptural authorship, historical identities, Quranic attribution or Aramaic validity. Four authors are insufficient to estimate population reliability; same genre does not ensure perfect topic matching.
